value: compound eyes large, globose, projecting somewhat dorsally; ventral margin acutely rounded
eye: compound eyes, adult female holotype (Miocene amber fossil)
method: taxonomic description of a fossil specimen in amber
conditions: Description of the female holotype (INHS 10175), the only specimen: one adult in a piece of Miocene Dominican amber (La Toca region, near Santiago de los Caballeros, Santiago Province, Dominican Republic; Early Miocene, Burdigalian); the male is unknown and the species is monotypic. Bubbles and debris obscure the protarsus and dorsal terminalia and apical damage prevents measuring the abdomen; no eye damage is reported. The Abstract and Diagnosis carry no eye wording. The Remarks say Electrotettix is similar to Baeotettix in the large eyes projecting dorsally above the fastigium. Ocelli are mentioned only as landmarks for the frontal costa, with no description of their size or condition.

value: compound eyes dark brown to black, 2 times broader than longer, rounded in front
method: taxonomic description of preserved type specimens
conditions: Description of the male holotype (Mengla County, Wuxiangguangchang, Xishuangbanna, Yunnan, China; 21.92 N, 101.11 E; 21-24 Mar. 2019); one female paratype with the same data. The female Description lists only body size, abdominal colour, epiproct and a subgenital-plate notch and ends 'Others same as male', so it gives no separate eye account. The Diagnosis says the species is most similar to X. leshanensis 'in the compound eyes with a narrow band along the inner margin' and distinguishes it by 'the compound eyes with a prominent brown band along their inner margin on both sides', against 'a yellowish-white band along the inner margin' in X. leshanensis; Table 1 gives 'With brown band along inner margin' for X. xishangbanna. The paper has no Remarks section. The ocelli are described in a separate sentence ('Ocelli grayish white.').

value: apposition compound eyes with eucones and open rhabdom
eye: compound eyes, adult males and females (sections and TEM, numbers not stated)
method: scanning electron microscopy, paraffin sectioning, transmission electron microscopy and micro-CT of adult heads
conditions: Laboratory-reared adults (stock gifted by the Institute of Plant Protection, Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences, and Shanxi Agricultural University; reared on Alternanthera philoxeroides); no field locality. SEM used nine adult heads and prothoraxes, male and female combined; section and TEM numbers are not given. The Results confirm each element separately (apposition eyes, four cone cells forming eucones, open rhabdom, Fig. 5D). Results give 341.00 +/- 3.35 (male) and 345.22 +/- 4.48 (female) ommatidia, not significantly different, and call the eyes ellipsoid without interommatidial hair; the Discussion sentence says the eyes 'contains few ommatidia whose shape is irregular', which reads against those counts. No facet diameter or rhabdom length value is reported.

value: eyes extremely reduced in size; dorsally divided by about 20 times the dorsal width of one eye
eye: compound eyes, adults (species Diagnosis; holotype male and 11 paratypes of unstated sex)
method: taxonomic description of preserved type specimens
conditions: Diagnosis of the new species; the Description repeats the clause and adds 'ventral portion absent'. Holotype male (Guangxi, Jinxiu County, Yinshan Conservation Station, beech forest, 1200 m, 11 July 2014) and 11 paratypes of unstated sex from three Jinxiu County sites (950-1300 m, July 2014). The Discussion reports that SEM showed the eye is not reduced completely, with only few ommatidia recognizable, and that the whole lateral part of the head is reduced; E. nigra Hansen (Borneo) has well-developed eyes divided dorsally by 4.4 times the dorsal width of one eye, and both species are apterous. The genus redescription says eyes are well developed and strongly constricted laterally, or largely reduced. No facet count is given.

value: compound eyes well developed, large, widely rounded, medially contiguous
eye: compound eyes, male imago holotype (amber fossil)
method: taxonomic description of a fossil specimen in amber
conditions: Description of the male imago holotype (BU-179). Both holotypes come from Hukawng Valley amber (Kachin State, Myanmar; exact mine unknown), Upper Albian (maximum age 98.79 ± 0.62 Ma, 'equivalent to the earliest Cenomanian'; the type lines print 'Cenomanian, mid-Cretaceous'), held in the State Museum of Natural History Stuttgart; each species rests on its one holotype and the paper mentions no other specimens. The same Description sentence goes on to give the colour of the upper and lower eye portions; the ocelli are 'poorly preserved, relatively small' in a separate sentence; the facets are hexagonal. The female holotype of B. clypeata has eyes 'widely separated medially' (distance between eyes 0.73 of head width). The paper does not exclude that the two holotypes are one species ('We do however not per se exclude a possible conspecifity of both fossil specimens.'), citing similar small body size and male/female proportions and the clypeus, and separates them by wing venation; the eye difference between this male and the B. clypeata female may therefore be sexual, and the paper does not compare the eyes. The Affinities eye wording concerns only the female, whose anterior eye portion is partly covered by the clypeal shield.

method: taxonomic description of a fossil specimen in amber
conditions: Description of the female imago holotype (BU-321). Both holotypes come from Hukawng Valley amber (Kachin State, Myanmar; exact mine unknown), Upper Albian (maximum age 98.79 ± 0.62 Ma, 'equivalent to the earliest Cenomanian'; the type lines print 'Cenomanian, mid-Cretaceous'), held in the State Museum of Natural History Stuttgart; each species rests on its one holotype and the paper mentions no other specimens. The same Description gives the distance between eyes as 0.73 of head width, says the clypeus is expanded anterolaterally and partly covers the anterior part of the eyes, and describes the ocelli as well preserved and large in a separate sentence. The male holotype of B. paucivenosa has compound eyes medially contiguous; the paper does not exclude that the two holotypes are one species ('We do however not per se exclude a possible conspecifity of both fossil specimens.'; the expanded clypeus 'may not exclude their conspecifity') and separates them by wing venation, so the eye difference may be sexual; the paper does not compare the eyes. The genus diagnosis gives 'in female (p) anterior part of eyes covered by anterolaterally expanded clypeal shield.'
